title: Linux Networking Building Blocks
summary: Network namespaces connect through veth pairs to a bridge; ip_forward and iptables NAT route traffic out, and keepalived provides a floating IP.

nodes.label: Namespace A
nodes.detail: A network namespace has its own interfaces, routes and firewall rules. Containers use one each.

nodes.label: Namespace B
nodes.detail: A second namespace with its own address, connected to the same bridge.

nodes.label: veth Pair A
nodes.detail: One end sits in the namespace, the other attaches to the bridge in the host namespace.

nodes.label: veth Pair B
nodes.detail: Pairs always carry packets from one end to the other.

nodes.label: Linux Bridge
nodes.detail: Forwards Ethernet frames between attached veth ends by MAC address, giving the namespaces one subnet.

nodes.label: Routing
nodes.detail: With net.ipv4.ip_forward enabled, the kernel forwards packets between interfaces using the routing table.

nodes.label: iptables NAT
nodes.detail: The POSTROUTING MASQUERADE rule rewrites private source addresses to the uplink address; DNAT can publish ports inward.

nodes.label: Uplink NIC
nodes.detail: Physical interface connecting the host to the outside network.

nodes.label: keepalived VRRP
nodes.detail: Moves a virtual IP between hosts using VRRP, for example to keep a gateway address highly available.

steps.title: Namespaces isolate stacks
steps.text: Each namespace has independent interfaces, routes and firewall rules.

steps.title: veth pairs link to the bridge
steps.text: The host-side end of each pair is plugged into a Linux bridge, acting as a switch.

steps.title: Routing forwards packets
steps.text: Namespaces use the bridge address as gateway; ip_forward lets the kernel route between interfaces.

steps.title: NAT rewrites sources
steps.text: iptables MASQUERADE translates private addresses so replies return through the uplink.

steps.title: VRRP floats the gateway
steps.text: keepalived can move a virtual gateway IP to a standby host on failure.
